message.content: {"thought": "The hardware candidate with nop_bw increased from 128 to 256 GB/s has been materialized. The updated hardware has 16 WS chiplets with 16384 compute units, 8192 buffer, 64 DRAM BW, 256 NoP BW, tp=16. This targets the communication-bound layers (res1 at 54.4% communication, res2 at 46.0% communication, norm2 at 33.4% communication) on the critical path. The monetary cost increase from IO (currently 12.3%) should be modest, while the latency reduction from faster NoP communication could significantly reduce the critical path end time (19.70s). The compute-bound FFN layers (67.6% of time) are already at max compute_units and won't be affected, but the memory/communication layers on the critical path should see improvement. I have sufficient evidence to propose this as the next hardware update.
